answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies can rest on a staked-identity registry: to transact, an agent must post a bond held in escrow that the protocol slashes on proven duplicate-identity linkage. Forging a thousand identities means funding a thousand independent bonds, so cost grows linear in identity count while payoff per fake account stays flat, and one deposit cannot be recycled. A thread of verified stake ties each account to real capital, and a velvet audit trail exposes duplicated votes before they pay out, pushing inflation toward a zenith where marginal cost matches credibility.
